free_tier.stated: 150 GB per uploaded file — raised from a lower value in the Python SDK on 2026-03-24 ('Increase upload file size limit to 150GB'). No published per-account or total quota anywhere in the provider terms, FAQ, or API reference; the archive in the public catalogue runs to multi-GB objects (one measured dataset is 9,786,006,314 bytes = 9.79 GB as a single .tar.gz). Uploads are multipart with a hard 10,000-part ceiling, so a 1 TB object would need ≥100 MB parts — the SDK enforces this and names the minimum part size rather than failing mid-upload.

egress.terms: Free to the consumer; storage is Cloudflare R2 in the EU plus AWS in Ireland per their own subprocessor table. Downloads are short-lived presigned URLs, and downloads are rate-limited to 30 per organisation per day (429 beyond that).

tooling: Best-in-slot for a scripted pipeline: a documented REST API at https://mozilladatacollective.com/api (bearer API key), plus a first-party Python SDK with resumable multipart uploads, configurable part_size and max_workers, and a .mdc-sample-upload.json resume-state file. Verified live: GET /api/health -> 200 (15 bytes), GET /api/datasets?limit=1 -> 200 with full metadata including sizeBytes and a SHA-256 checksum field.
chaining: One dataset = one submission = one archive file plus one sample file. Nothing in the published terms caps the number of submissions per account, so the multiplier is submissions. The catalogue is browsable and enumerable anonymously through /api/datasets, which means the read side can be driven entirely from a script.

limits_note: write-gated, hard. 'we manually review every request to upload' — you file a Request to Upload, wait days, and are interviewed by email about 'yourself, the organization you are representing, the data you want to upload and what are your goals'. They also ask for a full legal name and an organisation email. Every dataset must carry a datasheet. API upload calls are rate-limited at their discretion and skipping the approval flow ends the account. Also note the published conditions exclude rehosting or re-distributing datasets, which is a policy limit on using MDC as a mirror.
reliability_note: The gate is a human reviewer, not a form — treat acceptance as the scarce resource. 30 downloads/day/org will throttle any mirroring plan. Hash field is present in metadata, so a checksum roundtrip is cheap to automate.

extras.agent_focus: 2026-era research-data and data-marketplace platforms, deliberately judged on the BINDING constraint (does a person with only an email get past the write gate?) rather than on the marketing quota. Coverage: IEEE DataPort (the wave-7 discovery this slot confirms and extends), Mozilla Data Collective (2025 launch, the only new ≥100 GB-per-file free host found), Source Cooperative re-probed at the byte level, the French national Dataverse (Recherche Data Gouv) as the one genuinely EU-funded space with a self-serve email account, plus the 2026 data-marketplace entrants (Snowflake, Databricks Free Edition, data.world, Datarade, Tableland, Spice.ai, DataChain), the EU Data Spaces (Gaia-X / Catena-X / EOSC EU Node / DICE) and ResearchGate/Academia.edu data upload. Two structural results dominate: (a) the 'data marketplace' category is uniformly not storage — they are catalogues, and every one of them fails on per-object size by two to three orders of magnitude; (b) the EU Data Spaces are real and large but gated on eduGAIN/eIDAS identity, so they are closed on identity exactly like CSC Allas and LUMI-O before them.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
